summary: Ramp is a corporate card and spend management platform that Sacra estimates reached $1.5B in annualized revenue in May 2026, and multiple independent sources report it has been free-cash-flow positive since late 2025. Bloomberg reported a roughly $60B valuation in a round led by Dragoneer and Thrive Capital, following a $44B round co-led by ICONIQ, GIC and Ontario Teachers'. The verdict is pursue because independent sources back strong revenue growth, customer growth and funding from known investors, and the main risks are competition and international product gaps rather than legal or financial threats.

facts.text: Sacra estimates Ramp reached $1.5B in annualized revenue in May 2026, up from about $1.2B at the end of 2025.

evidence.quote: Sacra estimates that Ramp hit $1.5B in annualized revenue in May 2026, up from ~$1.2B at the end of 2025

facts.text: Ramp's total payments volume rose to $57B in 2024 from $22.3B in 2023, with net annualized revenue up 133% year over year.

evidence.quote: Ramp exited 2024 with net annualized revenue up 133% year over year as total payments volume (TPV) rose to $57B from $22.3B in 2023

facts.text: Ramp raised $750M at a $44B post-money valuation in June 2026, co-led by ICONIQ, GIC and the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan.

evidence.quote: Ramp raised $750M at a $44B post-money valuation in June 2026, with ICONIQ Capital, Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC, and the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan co-leading

evidence.quote: Dragoneer Investment Group and Thrive Capital led the round, with Founders Fund also contributing a large check

facts.text: Ramp has been generating positive free cash flow since late 2025, as reported by Sacra, The Next Web and PM Insights.

evidence.quote: the company was generating free cash flow as of November 1, 2025
Valued at $32B with $1B+ annualized revenue, positive free cash flow in 2025

facts.text: Sacra reports Ramp had 70,000+ business customers by June 2026, up from 50,000 at the start of the year; the company's own careers page claims 85,000+.

evidence.quote: By June 2026, Ramp reported 70,000+ business customers, up from 50,000 at the beginning of the year
The result? 85,000+ companies—from family farms to Shopify—saving billions of dollars and hours each year

facts.text: About 2,200 customers each contributed $100K+ in annualized revenue as of November 2025.

evidence.quote: As of November 2025, 2,200 customers were contributing $100K+ in annualized revenue
Generates $100K+ annual recurring revenue from 2,200+enterprise accounts

facts.text: Ramp is expanding beyond cards into bill pay, treasury and a stablecoin account partnership with Open USD for payments in more than 140 countries.

risks.text: Ramp faces crowded competition from Brex, American Express, Navan, Expensify, SAP Concur, Bill.com, Airbase, Mercury, Airwallex, Payhawk, Spendesk and Pleo.

evidence.quote: The best Ramp alternatives for SaaS companies are Brex, Airbase (now Maxio), Mercury, Airwallex, Payhawk, Spendesk, Navan, Teampay, and Pleo

risks.text: Ramp's international coverage is limited, with reviewers saying it does not issue cards in Canada, the UK or EU markets, pushing multi-entity companies to rivals.

evidence.quote: As of their public product pages, Ramp does not issue cards in Canada, the UK, or EU markets, and physical cards for non-US employees require workarounds that create friction for finance teams

risks.text: Users report recurring frustration with customer support responsiveness and the depth of AP automation and ERP integrations.

evidence.quote: ERP integration depth is another common complaint
Praised for AI-driven spend controls and clean UX, but support responsiveness and AP automation depth are recurring frustrations

risks.text: Revenue is predominantly tied to payments activity, and upmarket growth comes with modest take-rate compression.

evidence.quote: Revenue is predominantly tied to payments activity, while growth is being driven by multi-product penetration that increases wallet share per customer and routes more spend onto Ramp, plus deeper upmarket wins that carry higher absolute TPV even with modest take-rate compression

risks.text: Valuation has climbed very quickly, from $7.65B in April 2024 to $44B in June 2026, raising the bar for future returns.
